subject.title: fix(auth-health): prefer usable OAuth over expired inventory in provider status

question: Should provider-level OAuth status ever report ok or expiring when one effective OAuth profile is healthy but another effective OAuth profile is missing?
rationale: Masking missing auth changes the operator-visible auth-provider warning contract, and repository policy treats auth/provider status precedence as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Preserve Missing Warnings
options.body: Keep missing ahead of the healthy override and limit this PR to expired stale inventory, then require focused tests and real behavior proof.

options.title: Accept Healthy Masks Missing
options.body: Allow healthy OAuth to mask missing inventory, but record that contract in tests and maintainer-visible rationale before merge.

options.title: Pause For Canonical Scope
options.body: Hold this PR until maintainers decide whether the canonical stale-badge issue needs this rollup change, the cache-refresh PR, or both.

recommendation.title: Preserve Missing Warnings
recommendation.body: Keep missing ahead of the healthy override and limit this PR to expired stale inventory, then require focused tests and real behavior proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has recent history in the auth-health/status boundary and is a good owner for the precedence contract question.
